MESSAGE
Loan portfolio reached VND1.75 quadrillion, growing by 16.66%, 
accounting for about 13% of the total credit outstanding of the 
entire economy, leading the market in credit market share. The 
credit structure shifted towards sustainability, with the proportion 
of retail, SME and FDI loans to total outstanding loans reaching 
68.7%, a 1.2% increase compared to 2022. Credit quality was kept 
under controlled, with the non-performing loan ratio under Circular 
11 at 1.12%. Business efficiency showed positive growth compared 
to the previous year, achieving and surpassing the set targets for 
2023: (i) Consolidated net operating income reached VND47,932 
billion. Consolidated profit before tax reached VND27,589 billion, a 
growth of 20.4%, surpassing the plan set by the General Meeting 
of Shareholders; (ii) Financial capacity improved, with charter 
capital reaching VND57,004 billion. After 10 years of listing on the 
stock market, BIDV's market capitalization ranked among the top 
market leaders, surpassing USD10 billion; (iii) Profitability indicators 
improved positively compared to the previous year: ROA reached 
0.99%; ROE reached 19.36%; (iv) Provision was sufficient as per 
regulations, with a coverage ratio of bad debts reaching 183%, 
ensuring risk ratios complied with regulations and good practices. 
BIDV has also been one of the active contributors to the state 
budget with a contribution of over VND6,448 billion.
Empowering a green future
Recognizing the inevitable trend of long-term sustainable 
development, BIDV, as a leading financial institution in supporting 
the country's economic development, has steadfastly pursued 
the goal of becoming a "green bank" in the 2021-2025 business 
strategy and the vision towards 2030: (i) Issuing Resolutions to 
implement National Strategies for Green Growth and Climate 
Change Response, focusing on ESG practices through establishing 
an ESG Action Program, establishing specialized ESG management 
units according to international standards and practices, actively 
spreading the message of sustainable financial development to 
customers, partners...; (ii) Being the first joint-stock commercial 
bank in Vietnam to announce the "Sustainable Loan Framework" 
and professionalizing environmental and social risk management 
Dear valued customers, shareholders and partners,
The global economy in 2023 experienced complex and unpredictable 
developments, presenting many challenges beyond forecasts; 
financial, currency, and real estate markets carried significant risks; 
import-export activities declined, prolonged impacts from the 
Covid-19 pandemic, geopolitical tensions... Against that backdrop, 
Vietnam remained a bright spot in the overall economic landscape 
with some positive results: GDP growth reached 5.05%, among the 
highest levels in the region; the average consumer price index was 
kept under control at 3.25%; trade surplus reached USD28 billion. 
Among these collective successes, we must acknowledge the 
proactive and flexible monetary policy approach by the State Bank 
of Vietnam (SBV), alongside the synchronized implementation of 
measures to alleviate difficulties for businesses, promote economic 
growth, control inflation, and ensure the stability of the banking 
system. In 2023, SBV cut the policy rate four times by 0.5-2% to help 
improve the economy, thereby reducing the deposit and lending 
interest rates; managing exchange rates appropriately; refining 
regulations in banking activities, improving access to credit for 
enterprises and individuals, and achieving a credit growth rate for 
the entire industry of 13.78% in 2023.
Overcoming difficulties for rapid transformation
For BIDV, 2023 was of great significance as it marked the pivotal 
year of the 2021-2025 Business Development Strategy amidst 
numerous challenges. With unity, consensus, and concerted efforts, 
BIDV made 2023 a year of "rapid transformation". BIDV continued 
to affirm its leading position and role in effectively implementing 
monetary policies, contributed to maintaining the stability of the 
banking system; actively accompanied and supported enterprises 
and retail customers in line with the Government's and SBV's 
guidelines to promote economic recovery and development. 
By the end of 2023, BIDV's total assets reached over VND2.3 
quadrillion, maintaining its position as the largest commercial bank 
in Vietnam; mobilized capital from organizations and individuals 
reached VND1.89 quadrillion, increasing by 16.5%, accounting for 
approximately 14% of the total deposit market share of the entire 
industry. 
through the issuance of the "Environmental-Social Risk Management 
Framework", laying the foundation for providing customers with 
sustainable financial products according to international standards; 
(iii) Pioneering in attracting sustainable development capital, 
shifting towards a green economy, leading the market in green credit 
financing; being the first bank to successfully issue VND2.5 trillion 
green bonds according to international standards; (iv) Collaborating 
with various forums, seminars to share experiences and spread 
the message of sustainable development to customers, partners: 
Renewable Energy Conference 2023; Investment Opportunities 
in Renewable Energy Conference; Roundtable on Promoting 
Sustainable Energy Infrastructure Investment...
Pioneering the digital transformation journey
BIDV recognizes that technological innovation is a key factor in 
achieving sustainable development goals, enhancing competitive 
capacity, improving the quality of products and services, and 
meeting the increasing needs of customers. Alongside the digital 
transformation activities in the financial banking sector, in 2023, 
BIDV also made significant strides, affirming its pioneering position 
in the digital transformation journey: (i) Officially launching the Core 
Banking Profile system, integrating more than 100 applications into 
the core banking system, expecting comprehensive breakthroughs, 
especially in direction, business development strategy, product and 
service development mindset, organizational model, operational 
procedures... contributing to enhancing product and service quality, 
increasing customer satisfaction; (ii) Developing the Payment 
Hub system to plan and build an international-standard payment 
system - this is the largest and most complex technology project 
ever implemented using 100% internal resources of BIDV; (iii) Being 
the first bank to introduce the BIDV OPEN API system serving the 
open banking model with over 3,000 API-connected partners; 47 
payment intermediaries, public services, the State Treasury, Social 
Insurance...
Fostering institutional development for agility and efficiency
By the end of 2023, BIDV also achieved many advancements in 
management and governance, institutional development, laying a 
solid foundation for implementing the 2021-2025 business strategy 
and component strategies, towards sustainable development: (i) 
Firmly adhering to the overall development goals and targets of the 
Strategy until 2025, vision until 2030 and 07 component strategies... 
regularly, meticulously evaluating and thereby proposing key 
solutions to ensure the correct implementation direction; (ii) 
Continuing to optimize the organizational structure at all levels: 
Re-establishing the Retail Banking Division and restructuring units 
within the Division; Establishing the Asset Valuation Center, the Hi-
tech R&D Center in Ho Chi Minh City...; (iii) Strengthening strategic 
cooperation with multilateral institutions to enhance customer 
service capacity, system management capacity, especially premier 
and private customer services making a mark with the establishment 
of a strategic partnership with Edmond de Rothschild - a leading 
global financial institution in investment and asset management, 
bringing high-end financial services opportunities to premier and 
private customers on a global scale; (iv) Continuing institutional 
reforms towards intensifying administrative procedure reforms, 
streamlining business processes, enhancing efficiency, labor 
productivity across the entire system.
The aforementioned success of BIDV is the result of the concerted 
efforts of nearly 30,000 employees, who have tirelessly worked day 
and night. As a result, in 2023, BIDV continued to be highly regarded 
by organizations and communities, receiving prestigious awards: 
ranking 1,081st - up more than 500 places in the Forbes Global 
2000 list of the largest public companies worldwide; the "Top 50 
Best Listed Companies" award (Forbes Vietnam magazine); "Best 
Retail Bank in Vietnam" for nine consecutive years, "Best Private 
Banking Service in Vietnam", "Best International Credit Card in 
Vietnam", "Best FX Provider in Vietnam", and "Best Custodian Bank 
in Vietnam in 2023" (The Asian Banker); "Best SME Bank in Vietnam" 
award (Alpha Southeast Asia); the "Leading Digital Banking Solution 
Provider in Vietnam" award (Asiamoney); nine BIDV IT products 
winning the Sao Khue Award 2023; and among the Top 10 Excellent 
Brands of Vietnam 2023 (Vietnam Economic Times)...
Streamlining processes, transforming operations
2024 marks a year of acceleration and breakthrough, holding 
particular significance in achieving the five-year business strategy 
goals. BIDV has identified the guiding principle for the year as 
"Streamlining processes - Transforming operations". Accordingly, 
BIDV will comprehensively, cohesively, and substantively transform 
all activities, with a strong and fundamental shift starting from 
perception, goal-oriented planning, business model, to operational 
models 
oriented 
towards 
sustainable 
development 
(ESG). 
Firmly committed to eliminating redundancies, improving, and 
simplifying processes, cutting costs, enhancing labor productivity 
and customer service capabilities coupled with the application of 
technology through the internal management system (B.One). 
Focused measures to expand operational scale are linked with 
stringent credit quality control, improving asset quality, and 
restructuring the customer base... Enhancing operational efficiency 
is tied to transitioning income structure towards increasing non-
interest income; enhancing managerial and risk management 
capabilities; focusing on implementing capital increase plans to 
enhance financial capacity and business development.
On behalf of the BIDV Board of Directors, I would like to extend sincere 
gratitude to all the leadership team and nearly 30,000 employees 
who have dedicated themselves to BIDV. In particular, I would like to 
express deep appreciation to our valued Customers, Investors, and 
Partners who have continuously placed trust in and accompanied 
BIDV throughout this journey. We look forward to continuing our 
cooperation and partnership with you, our esteemed customers, 
investors, and partners, to collectively create sustainable values, 
aiming towards a prosperous and thriving future!

MAIN AND PROMINENT PRODUCTS
WHOLESALE BANKING GROUP
Supply Chain Financing
With the goal of making BIDV to become the number one bank in 
supply chain finance, with the goal of achieving a supply chain finance 
scale of USD1.6 billion by 2026, in the past time, BIDV has allocated 
many resources to invest in product development, application of 
information technology, and sales. With the ability to provide "tailor-
made" solutions for many large enterprises, BIDV has collaborated 
to build supply chain finance programs for leading corporations 
in economic sectors such as real estate, fast-moving consumer 
goods (FMCG), automobile distribution, electrical equipment. 2023 
also recorded BIDV's successes in conquering central businesses, 
multinational corporations as well as large domestic conglomerates 
through solutions regarding products, digital technology applications, 
and promotion policies with many preferential resources for supply 
chain customers. 
With synchronized solutions, in 2023, the balance of supply chain 
financing credits increased nearly threefold compared to 2022. In 
which, the number of SMEs in Vietnam accessing supply chain 
financing from BIDV increased by 195%, and the disbursement speed 
through this solution also increased by 123% over the past year.
Digital Banking for corporate customers
With the goal of becoming the best digital platform bank in Vietnam, BIDV has continuously 
strived to build a comprehensive digital banking ecosystem for corporate customers 
through 2 platforms: Omni BIDV iBank and BIDV iConnect. 
In 2023, BIDV continuously expanded and improved its digital banking system, especially the 
BIDV iBank application, to provide seamless experiences and optimize financial solutions for 
customers with features including international money transfer, foreign currency exchange, 
and online term deposit products.BIDV iBank and BIDV iConnect have become the main 
pillars in the bank's digital ecosystem, contributing significantly to creating sustainable 
value for customers.
At the same time, to meet the Government's strategic goal of digitizing and optimizing 
administrative procedures to provide convenience to citizens, BIDV actively deployed online 
fee collection services for government agencies on the National Public Service Portal. 
Outstandingly in 2023, the fee payment service for university entrance exam fees was 
vigorously promoted with nearly 63,500 transactions conducted in 3 months of deployment, 
reaching a total value of VND6.88 billion. In 2023, the number of public service transactions 
deployed via BIDV reached nearly 800,000 transactions, a growth of 445% compared to 
2022. 
The development of the digital ecosystem also became one of the areas of interest for 
BIDV. On November 29, 2023, BIDV pioneered the launch of the BIDV Open API system to 
the market - an open ecosystem to integrate banking services into customers' applications, 
software, and digital platforms. With BIDV Open API, banking services will be most easily 
integrated into applications, software, and digital platforms in the market, creating new 
financial solutions, enhancing the experience for individual and corporate customers in 
shopping, payment, business, and financial management in the digital space. Developing 
products focusing on enhancing customer experience, BIDV's digital products have been 
positively received by the business community.
Trade Finance
In addition to service incentives, BIDV has always given priority to 
extending credit to import-export businesses through preferential 
credit packages with flexible credit conditions. BIDV has also 
launched diverse trade finance products with flexible collateral 
conditions such as unsecured loans, mortgage of receivables 
from export contracts, imported shipments, etc. to timely meet the 
demand of businesses. In particular, international payment and 
trade finance products and services have been digitized, allowing 
business customers to send transaction documents, receive and 
track processing results via BIDV iBank.
BIDV's portfolio of trade finance products is comprehensive, diverse 
in accordance with international standards and practices such as 
letter of credit (L/C), collection, negotiation of bill of exchange, 
forfaiting... The bank has great advantages in its wide network of 
correspondent banks/international payment markets to deploy and 
provide the trade finance service to customers.
Industry credit
BIDV designs, improves credit product packages by industry as 
well as comprehensive solutions, packaging of service products 
(all-in-one) to best meet the needs of customers in each industry, 
economic sector. BIDV prioritizes credit promotion for potential 
industries crucial to the economy such as industrial park real 
estate, renewable energy, import-export sectors, pharmaceuticals, 
construction.BIDV is also a pioneering bank in implementing credit 
solutions to contribute to the implementation and guidance of the 
Party and the Government in the recovery and development of the 
economy, through the implementation of the VND120 trillion credit 
program for social housing, worker housing loans, renovation, 
reconstruction of old apartment buildings under Resolution 33/
NQ-CP, Credit package for commercial real estate sector suitable 
for actual housing needs in the market or credit program for the 
forestry, fisheries sectors and so on.
Green credit
BIDV is the first joint-stock commercial bank in Vietnam to 
announce the "Sustainable Financing Framework" and is currently 
the market leader in financing green projects with thousands of 
customers and projects. Always in the Top 5 banks with the largest 
green credit balances in the system, as of 31 December, 2023, 
BIDV's green credit balance reached VND74,177 billion (accounting 
for 4.24% of the total balance), mainly focusing on the renewable 
energy sector, clean energy with a balance of VND60,092 billion 
(accounting for 81% of the total green credit balance). More than 
just a bank, BIDV pioneered the development of sustainable 
financial products by successfully implementing the Green Textile 
product alongside a VND4,200 billion Green credit package to 
provide significant support for textile enterprises to transform their 
business operations towards sustainable development.

Green Credit - Leading the trend
In response to the National Strategy on Green Growth for the 
period 2021 - 2030, with a vision to 2050, besides preferential loan 
packages such as personal instalment loans, traditional production 
and business loans, BIDV issued a Green Credit Package for 
individual customers for the development of clean energy (solar 
power, wind power) or for farming and raising livestock following 
the standards of VIETGAP, ISO, with more attractive and preferential 
interest rate policies.
In addition, BIDV also focused on digitizing processes, credit 
product dossiers and reducing paperwork and paper records to 
become the first state-owned bank deploying credit extension on all 
digital platforms with appraisal and approval process on the RLOS 
system.
Besides, the online BIDV Home loan application continued to be 
improved and upgraded to complete the customer journey through 
finding out information, registering for a loan to receive preferential 
interest rates, sending documents directly through the application 
and tracking loan processing progress online. The application 
also offers various options through connecting with reputable 
partners, providing green housing projects, and car lines using 
environmentally friendly electric engines for customers.
BIDV SmartBanking – A comprehensive 
digital financial ecosystem
BIDV SmartBanking has become a digital financial ecosystem that 
fully meets customer needs, which not only provides essential 
services but also resolves advanced financial needs. With that 
orientation, BIDV has digitized over 60% of traditional products 
(deposits, loans, cards, international money transfers...), while

1. ECONOMIC RISK
In 2023, the international economic environment continued to 
recover slowly, unstably and unevenly due to: 
 •	
Increasing and unpredictable geopolitical conflicts
 •	
Governments and central banks of countries continued to 
implement tight monetary policies, increase and keep interest rates 
at high levels, to cope with inflation, which reduced world demand, 
leading to stagnation in the manufacturing sector in many large 
economies such as Germany and Japan, causing these countries 
to face the risk of recession or falling into a technical recession in 
the short term
 •	
Financial - currency risk, food security risk, energy security and 
supply chain risks increased.
The domestic economy in 2023 saw bright spots: macroeconomic 
balances were ensured, inflation was well controlled at 3.25%, 
exchange rates increased but were still under control, interest 
rates continued to decrease, the economic growth rate was quite 
good at 5.05% (although lower than the target of 6-6.5%, it was an 
encouraging level, ranking third in the ASEAN region, just behind 
Cambodia (5.4%) and Philippines (5.6%)) 
However, the economy faced great difficulties and challenges 
such as: 
 •	
Lingering external risks and challenges
 •	
Traditional growth drivers (exports, final consumption, industrial 
production, private investment) recovered slowly, growth quality did 
not improve
 •	
Business activities continued to face many difficulties (both in 
terms of output, capital absorption and access)
 •	
Credit growth was slow, bad debt increased
 •	
Restructuring of the economy and weak businesses was still 
slow, regulations for new growth engines were still slow to be 
promulgated
 •	
Corporate bond, real estate and gold markets still posed risks.
In 2023, given the difficulties and challenges both international and 
domestic, BIDV always proactively analyzed, promptly evaluated 
and developed scenarios to flexibly respond to rapid and abnormal 
changes in the market, on the basis of compliance with the 
operating policies of the Government, the State Bank of Vietnam 
and competent agencies; thereby, helping BIDV's operations be 
safe, smooth and effective.
In 2024, risks and challenges from the international context are 
forecast to include:
 •	
Lingering and unpredictable geopolitical conflicts, continuing to 
impact global production and supply chains
 •	
Although inflation is cooling down, central banks of countries are 
expected not to continue raising interest rates, and that interest 
rates in the US and Europe will still remain high until inflation is 
controlled and lowered gradually towards the target level
 •	
Many world’s economic locomotives are weak (the EU economy is 
forecast to fall into a technical recession) or recover more slowly than 
expected (the US economy is forecast to grow by 2.1% (according 
to the IMF, compared with 2.5% in 2023), China's economic recovery 
has not yet created a spillover to other economies...), causing the 
global economy to continue to grow slowly (about 2.4% in 2024 
(according to WB’s January 2024) or 3.1% (according to IMF’s 
January 2024)
 •	
Increased savings and defensive sentiments cause a decline in 
demand for goods and services, affecting the export, manufacturing 
and tourism sectors in many countries
 •	
Climate change with harsh and extreme weather (natural disasters, 
flooding, droughts...) hinders the economic recovery in many 
countries and regions.
Some internal risks and challenges of Vietnam's economy in 2024 
include: 
 •	
The international economy recovers slowly; some regions and 
countries, especially Vietnam's major trading partners grow slowly 
or may fall into a technical recession, reducing demand for exports, 
investment, consumption and international tourism
 •	
Unresolved bottlenecks such as the economic growth model, the 
economic structure is still unreasonable, the quality of growth is not

 •	
Challenges from implementing new FTAs, especially pressures on

 •	
Vietnam is still lagged behind in the trend of developing technology

 •	
The aging population, the rise of the middle class and the 
development of science and technology require political institutions 
to be more transparent and accountable
 •	
Vietnam is negatively impacted by climate change and 
environmental pollution.
Accordingly, Vietnam's economy is forecast to grow at about 6-6.5% 
(according to the base scenario) and inflation to be controlled at 
about 3.5-4% in 2024.
With international and domestic economic prospects being

to complete its business plan with motto “Streamlining processes 
- Transforming operations”, seriously implementing the orientation 
of the Government and SBV, ensuring the BIDV system operates

system and national economy.

Therefore, Vietnam's legal system has constantly been developed

The legal system and economic policies have been developed 
uniformly in line with market mechanisms, meeting certain 
development 
requirements 
of 
the 
market 
economy 
and 
international integration. In recent years, the National Assembly 
of Vietnam has adopted important laws aimed at improving the 
legal framework for business environment and operation of credit 
institutions in Vietnam, including: Bidding Law No. 22/2023/
QH15, Electronic Transaction Law No. 20/2023/QH15, Real Estate 
Business Law No. 29/2023/QH15, Housing Law No. 27/2023/
QH15, Price Law No. 16/ 2023/QH15, Water Resources Law No. 
28/2023/QH15, Telecommunications Law No. 24/2023/QH15, 
Land Law No. 31/2024/QH15. The newly issued regulations were 
evaluated to be practical, suitable with the changes of the current 
business environment and have created fundamental changes in 
the operations of businesses in general and BIDV in particular.
Regarding the handling of bad debt, Resolution No.42/2017/
QH14 (Resolution 42) on piloting the handling of bad debt of credit 
institutions expired on 31 December 2023, meanwhile the 2015 
Civil Code, Decree No. 21/2021/ND-CP dated 19 March 2021 
regulating the implementation of the Civil Code on ensuring the 
performance of obligations no longer stipulate the mechanism for 
seizing collateral for handling. In 2023, credit institutions (including 
BIDV) contributed and providing inputs on building a mechanism 
to legalize Resolution 42 on piloting the handling of bad debt of 
credit institutions in the draft revised Law on Credit Institutions. 
However, the Law on Credit Institutions 2024 (effective from 1 July 
2024) adopted by the National Assembly has omitted and no longer 
stipulates the seizure of collateral. Accordingly, the bank no longer 
has a mechanism to proactively handle debt (seizing collateral) to 
shorten the time for recollecting bad debts as before. Therefore, the 
trend of applying lawsuit measures to recover loans and resolve 
disputes with customers is increasing in the number of cases and 
is prioritized so the handling of bad debt may take time and depend 
on the resolution procedures of the competent court.
Regarding dispute settlement in the fields of civil and commercial 
matters: Basically, the settlement of disputes at the court related 
to credit contracts and collateral ensured the legal and legitimate 
interests of credit institutions. In 2023, the Supreme People's Court 
issued Document No. 196/TANDTC-PC announcing the results of 
online answers to some problems in trial work ("Document 196”). 
Accordingly, the Supreme People's Court issued a unified guidance 
on judicial opinions for a number of legal situations arising directly/
related to banking activities such as mortgaging of savings books 
which beared the name of a spouse, effectiveness of a mortgage 
contract when there is a request to handle collateral in a credit 
contract dispute, the bank's right to choose collateral to handle in 
case an obligation is secured by many assets, the collateral being 
the right to use agricultural land, appraisal of collateral, handling 
of collateral being automobiles..., thereby facilitating banks in the 
proceeding process.
In addition, there still remained some cases where BIDV was a bona 
fide mortgagee in accordance with the law (receiving collateral 
based on the certificate of ownership issued by a competent 
authority without any dispute at the time of collateral acceptance), 
the Court still declared the mortgage transaction invalid because 
the previous asset transaction with a third party was declared 
invalid. On 2 August 2021, the Supreme People's Court issued 
Official Document No. 02/TANDTC-PC (“Document 02”) addressing 
trial issues. Accordingly, a guideline for judgment was directed to 
the court system with the following content: Credit institutions need 
to carry out procedures for appraisal and verification of the asset 
which serves as a basis to prove the actual owner of the asset, then 
a bona fide third party can be identified. This is also the point of view 
that credit institutions should pay attention to and learn from in the 
process of establishing new security relationships with customers. 
BIDV continues to work with commercial banks and Vietnam 
banks association to propose to the Supreme People's Court for 
reconsideration on a more favorable viewpoint for banks.
In addition, the Government and the State Bank of Vietnam 
also promulgated important Decrees and Circulars to guide the 
implementation of the provisions of law in the fields of finance and 
banking: Decree No. 08/2023/ND-CP amending, supplementing 
and suspending the implementation of a number of articles in 
Decrees on private placement and trading of corporate bonds 
in the domestic market and offering to the international market 
(Decree No. 153/2020/ND-CP and Decree 65/2022/ND-CP); 
Decree 23/2023/ND-CP amending and supplementing a number 
of Articles of Decree 89/2016/ND-CP on conditions for foreign 
currency exchange agency activities and provision of foreign 
currency receipt and payment services of economic organizations 
and Decree 88/2019/ND-CP regulating sanctions for administrative 
violations in the field of currency and banking; Circular 08/2023/
TT-NHNN dated 30 June 2023 regulating conditions on foreign 
loans not guaranteed by the Government, in replacement of Circular 
12/2014/TT-NHNN of the Governor of the State Bank; Circular 
22/2023/TT-NHNN amending and supplementing a number of 
Articles of Circular No. 41/2016/TT-NHNN on capital adequacy 
ratios for banks and foreign bank branches with specific provisions 
on determining and applying risk coefficients for each type of asset, 
including loans secured by real estate and home mortgage loans, 
clarifying and expanding conditions and regulations related to 
buying a house and mortgaging the very off-the-plan house.
On 28 June 2023, the Governor of the State Bank issued Circular

As a developing economy which has strongly integrated into the

Counterparty credit risk
Counterparty credit risk is the risk that arises when a counterparty 
fails to perform or is unable to fulfill part or all of payment 
obligation before or when the following transactions become due: 
(i) proprietary trading, (ii) Repo and reverse repos, (iii) Derivatives 
for hedging, (iv) Trading foreign currencies, financial assets for the 
purpose of serving the needs of customers and partners.
The counterparty credit risk management framework was carried 
out fully and uniformly, including:
 •	
Organizational structure with three lines of defense.
 •	
Developing and issuing a comprehensive system of regulations and 
documents in accordance with the State Bank’s regulations.
 •	
Having risk appetites, limits, and measurement tools in accordance 
with practices.
 •	
Having an IT system to support risk management.
The year 2023 marked the first time BIDV had a full system 
of documents on issuance and management of counterparty 
credit risk limits through the issuance of decentralization and 
separate policies for the issuance of counterparty credit risk 
limits. Regarding tool development, BIDV continued to deploy the 
calculation of counterparty credit risk-weighted assets according 
to the regulations of the State Bank of Vietnam in Circular 41 and 
piloted the SA-CCR method, and at the same time researching the 
counterparty credit risk management according to the internal 
model method (IMM) in order to approach Basel III.
In 2024, BIDV will: (i) continue to improve the system of regulations 
and documents for counterparty credit risk management, towards 
a comprehensive counterparty credit risk management framework; 
(ii) deploy tools for measurement and management of the 
counterparty credit risk according to advanced approach, ensuring 
compliance with the requirements of the State Bank and Basel 
standards; (iii) strengthen training, research and communication on 
counterparty credit risk management framework across the system 
and (iv) upgrade and develop programs and software, and boost the 
digital transformation in the counterparty credit risk management.

Sustainable loan framework
BIDV officially issued the "Sustainable Loan Framework" in 
consultation with the Carbon Trust. BIDV was the first Vietnamese 
commercial bank to announce the "Sustainable Loan Framework", 
which has laid foundations for the bank to develop sustainable 
financial products according to international standards.
BIDV's Sustainable Loan Framework was developed on the 
principles set by the Loan Market Association (LMA), the Loan 
Syndications and Trading Association (LSTA) and Asia Pacific 
Loan Market Association (APLMA), including Green Loan Principles 
(GLP); Social Loan Principles (SLP) and Sustainability-Linked 
Loan Principles (SLLP), as well as in accordance with current legal 
regulations and business situation in Vietnam.
BIDV's Sustainable loan framework was developed to offer the most 
popular sustainable loan products in the global market, including 
Thematic Loans and Sustainability Linked Loans. Thematic loans 
include Green Loans, Social Loans and Sustainable Loans, designed 
specifically for projects that use capital for environmental benefits 
(Green Loans), or social welfare (Social Loan), or both for social and 
environmental benefits (Sustainable Loan). Sustainability-linked 
loans include those that are designed to encourage the borrowers 
to achieve sustainability linked targets which are pre-agreed and 
measured through selected key performance indicators.
 •	
Management of proceeds from the bond issuance: Determining 
how the issuer manages the proceeds after issuance;
 •	
Post-issue reporting: Establishing reporting processes that need to 
be complied in the post-issue phase.
BIDV's green bond framework was assessed by Moody's as 
complying with the Green Bond Principles of the International 
Capital Market Association (ICMA) and scored at SQS2 (very good), 
thereby affirming BIDV’s high-level compliance and transparency 
in project selection, appraisal, lending, governance and reporting 
regimes when issuing green bonds.
Based on the Green Bond Framework, on 25 October 2023, BIDV 
successfully issued VND2,500 billion of 5-year bonds, becoming 
the first bank to issue green bonds according to the international 
standards in the domestic market.
BIDV's Sustainable Loan Framework also provides a clear 
framework for Thematic Loans and Sustainability-linked Loans. 
Accordingly, the thematic loan is determined based on four core 
components including: (i) Loan use purpose (ii) Process for project 
evaluation and selection; (iii) Management of loan use, and (iv) 
Reporting. Meanwhile, the Sustainability-linked loan is based on 
five pillars including: (i) Selecting Key Performance Indicators 
(KPI); (ii) Determining Sustainable Performance targets; (iii) Loan 
characteristics; (iv) Reporting, and (v) Third party verification.

INVESTOR RELATIONS
As a link between BIDV, shareholders and the investor community, the Investor Relations Division 
- Secretariat of the Board of Directors and Investor Relations works to protect shareholders' rights 
and interests in accordance with international standards, improve BIDV's reputation to attract 
new investors, receive and exchange information between the investor community and the Bank's 
Management.
Information transparency 
and protection of 
shareholders' interests
As a major public firm, BIDV always prioritizes accuracy, timeliness, and transparency in 
information disclosures. Up to this point, among state-owned banks, BIDV has been a leader 
in the disclosure of thorough and comprehensive information on all information disclosure 
systems of state agencies. Both Vietnamese and English versions of the information were 
fully published.
In 2023, BIDV disclosed 28 periodic contents and 186 extraordinary contents, including 
details on financial statements, 2021 annual reports, sustainable development reports, 
corporate governance report, invitations to general meetings of shareholders, collecting 
shareholders’ written opinions, information regarding insiders' retirement receiving social 
insurance benefits, information on transactions with related parties, bonds issuance, etc.
BIDV also makes a constant effort to broaden and improve information disclosure channels. 
Until now, the following methods have been used to communicate with shareholders and 
the investment community: Direct communication with shareholders at the annual general 
meeting; Information exchanged during meetings with investors and analysts; Information 
disclosure channels including the new BIDV website (which is user-friendly on mobile devices 
and has a number of new features), the Stock Exchange and State Securities Commission 
portals, the Ministry of Planning and Investment's enterprise portal, and publications like the 
annual report, the sustainable development report, the periodic newsletters for investors, 
among others.
The 2023 Annual General Meeting of Shareholders (AGM) was carefully convened by BIDV 
in accordance with current regulations in order to provide timely information on the Bank's 
performance for shareholders. Shareholders voted on significant matters pertaining to 
BIDV's operations during the 2023 Annual General Meeting of Shareholders, where they 
also asked direct questions and gave suggestions to the Bank’s Management based on the 
Reports and Proposals that were presented. The documents agreed by the general meeting 
of shareholders were fully uploaded on the investor page after the meeting, ensuring that 
all shareholders, including those who did not attend, could understand the crucial issues at 
the meeting.
With a varied and diversified group of shareholders, BIDV placed high priority on shareholder 
management to protect their interests. Via different channels, such as phone, email, or 
chatbot on the company website, the Investor Relations Department actively supported and 
responded to queries and requests from shareholders and investors in 2023, particularly 
retail shareholders and investors. The updating of shareholder information takes place 
swiftly, in line with rules, and in accordance with shareholders' needs and expectations.
Enhancing investor 
communication frequency 
and advancing the standard 
of market information
In 2023, with increased frequency, BIDV established and maintained productive connections 
with a significant number of domestic and international institutional investors. With expertise 
and insightful knowledge, investors provided helpful feedback, ideas, and proposals with 
true value for BIDV's operations.
In 2023, BIDV conducted 50 meetings and worked with more than 100 investors, including 
investment funds, recognized global financial institutions, investment banks, and securities 
firms from various countries and regions (USA, UK, Singapore, Italy, France, Hong Kong, 
Middle East, Vietnam, etc). Many partners and investors praised BIDV's performance and 
stock price despite macroeconomic challenges and stock market high volatility. Investors 
complimented BIDV for its professionalism and transparency of information for the 
numerous sessions it held to discuss complex macroeconomic issues, monetary policy, 
and corporate strategy. This makes it easier for analysts to understand the bank's business 
prospects for analysis, evaluation, and investment recommendation. The analyst reports 
for BIDV have greatly improved in 2023. Major securities firms have all advised investors to 
Buy/Increase/Outperform BID shares as a result.
Besides, BIDV also actively participated in domestic and foreign investment seminars 
and conferences such as Vietnam C-Suite Forum 2023 organized by Citi-SSI in February 
2023, Vietnam Access Days 2023 held by VietCapital in February 2023, Emerging Vietnam 
2023 held by HSC in June 2023, ASEAN Financials and Real Estate Investment Forum held 
by Citi Group in Singapore in August 2023. In addition to the quarterly update of BIDV's 
presentation for investors, BIDV also released the BIDV Newsletter for shareholders.
BIDV also developed, completed and issued the Manual of Code of Ethics in Investor 
Relations at BIDV and a set of case studies guiding the practice of the Manual of Professional 
Ethics in Investor Relations activities to adopt good practices. As one of the leading banks 
in the Vietnamese banking system and in the Top 5 largest market capitalization, BIDV 
always receives the wide attention of the public. After being promulgated, the manual of 
professional ethics has become a compass for officials performing investor relations work 
at BIDV.

BASIS OF CONSOLIDATION 
The accompanying consolidated financial statements, expressed in Vietnam Dong (VND), 
are prepared under the historical cost convention in accordance with Vietnamese Accounting 
Standards, accounting regime applicable to credit institutions in Vietnam and legal regulations 
relating to consolidated financial reporting. However, due to the Bank’s large scale of operations, 
for the purpose of preparing these consolidated financial statements, the figures are rounded to 
and presented in millions of Vietnam Dong (VND). This presentation does not materially affect the 
consolidated financial statements in terms of the consolidated financial position, the consolidated 
results of operations and the consolidated cash flows of the Bank and its subsidiaries. With regard 
to the number of shares and earnings per share, the Bank presented the items in unit position. 
The accompanying consolidated financial statements are not intended to present the consolidated 
financial position, consolidated income statement and consolidated cash flows in accordance with 
accounting principles and practices which are generally accepted in countries and jurisdictions 
other than Vietnam.
The consolidated financial statements incorporate the separate financial statements of the Bank and the financial statements of enterprises 
controlled by the Bank (its subsidiaries) for the year ended 31 December 2023. Control is achieved where the Bank has the power to govern 
the financial and operating policies of investee enterprises so as to obtain benefits from their activities.
The operating results of subsidiaries acquired or disposed of during the year are included in the consolidated income statement from the 
effective date of acquisition or up to the effective date of disposal, as appropriate. Where necessary, adjustments are made to the financial 
statements of subsidiaries to bring the accounting policies used in line with those used by the Bank. All internal transactions and balances 
between the Bank and its subsidiaries and among are eliminated in full on consolidation.
Non-controlling interests consist of the amount of those non-controlling interests at the date of the original business combination (see 
details below) and the non- controlling interests’ share of changes in equity since the date of the combination. Losses in subsidiaries are 
respectively attributed to the non-controlling interests even if these results in the non-controlling interests have a deficit balance.

including:

 •

 •

issued by other credit institutions) unlisted on the stock market or unregistered to be traded 
in the Unlisted Public Company Market (UPCoM) (hereinafter referred to as unlisted bonds), 
excluding entrusted capital sources for purchase of unlisted bonds whereby the entrusting 
parties bear risks;
 •

 •	
Deposits (except for current accounts, deposits at Vietnam Bank for Social Policies in 
accordance with the regulations of the SBV on maintaining balance of deposits at the social 
policy bank of state-owned credit institution) at other credit institutions, foreign banks’ 
branches as prescribed by law and making deposits at overseas credit institutions;

 •	
Repos of government bonds in the stock market in accordance with the provisions of law

Insurance incomes and

Direct premiums are recognized in accordance with Circular No. 50/2017/TT-BTC by the 
Ministry of Finance effective 01 July 2017 (Circular 50). Accordingly, direct premium income 
is recognized when the following conditions are met: (1) the agreement has been entered 
into by the insurer and the insured, who has paid premiums fully; (2) there is evidence that 
the insurance policy has been signed and the insured has paid the premiums fully; and 
(3) the insurance policy is signed and there is an agreement between the insurer and the 
insured for delayed payment of insurance premium, and in this case, the insurer will still 
record the premium amount as an income for the current year even though the amount 
has not been paid by the insured. The payment period is no longer than 30 days from the 
effective date of the insurance policy. 
In the case of the periodic payment, the insurer records income from insurance premiums 
of the first payment period when the contract is effective and only records revenue from 
insurance premiums of the next payment periods when the insured has fully paid the 
insurance premium as contract agreements. In case the insured has not fully paid the 
insurance premium according to the payment term, the insurance contract is automatically 
terminated at the end of the insurance premium payment term. The prepaid premium before 
the due date as at the consolidated balance sheet date is recognized in the “Other payables 
and liabilities” item in the consolidated balance sheet. 
Insurance claim expenses are recognized when the claim documents are completed and 
approved by the authorized person. In case that the final claim amount has not been 
finalized, but the insurer is certain that the loss is within its insured liabilities and has paid 
an advance to the customer as per their request, such advance would also be recognized 
as claim expense. The claims which have not been approved as at the consolidated balance 
sheet date are considered as outstanding claims and included in claim reserves.
The commission expense of each product is calculated as a percentage of the direct 
premium as stated in Circular 50. Commission expenses are allocated and recognized in 
the consolidated income statement corresponding with the premium earned.

Post-employment benefits
Severance allowance 
According to Article 46 of Labor Code 2019, the Bank and its subsidiaries in Vietnam are 
responsible to pay severance allowance for employees who have regularly worked at the 
Bank and its subsidiaries for 12 months or more, half-month salary allowance for each 
working year before 01 January 2009. The working period used for calculation of severance 
allowance excludes the period that employees benefit from unemployment insurance and 
the working period that employees receive severance allowance, retrenchment benefits 
from employers.
Retrenchment benefits
According to Article 47 of Labor Code 2019, the Bank and its subsidiaries in Vietnam are 
responsible to pay retrenchment benefits for employees who have regularly worked at the 
Bank and its subsidiaries for 12 months or more but are retrenched from their jobs as a 
result of organizational restructuring, technological changes, economic reasons, business 
combination, consolidation and split. For each year of employment, the employee is entitled 
to one-month salary but not less than two times the average salary of 06 consecutive 
months immediately preceding the job loss date. The working period used for calculation 
of retrenchment benefits excludes the period that employees benefit from unemployment 
insurance and the working period that employees receive severance allowance, retrenchment 
benefits from employers.
Unemployment insurance 
According to the Circular No. 28/2015/TT-BLDTBXH dated 31 July 2015 of the Ministry 
of Labor - War Invalids and Social Affairs guiding the implementation of Article 52 of the 
Employment Law 2013 and the Decree No. 28/2015/ND-CP of the Government dated 12 
March 2015 regulating the implementation of the Law on unemployment insurance, from 
01 January 2009, the Bank and its subsidiaries are obliged to pay unemployment insurance 
to eligible employees at 1% of their salary fund allocated for unemployment insurance.
